To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the matrix elements of the non-planar one-loop dilatation operator between operators dual to folding strings are of the form of an interaction vertex in a string field theory, and that the semi-classical contribution to the genus-one energy shift is suppressed.

the matrix elements of the dilatation operator for = 4 SY M between folded Frolov-Tsytlin strings have the form of a sum of terms of the form 1/(2n)! (where n is a positive integer), that the leading term in the sum is 1, and that the matrix elements are small.
we observe a curious scaling of matrix elements between folded strings and that the contribution to energy shift from semi-classical splitting and joining is suppressed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quasilocality of the dilatation operator in the planar limit.
the question whether the string world-sheet description of the gauge theory operators is valid at the level of matrix elements of the dilatation operator.
the quasilocality of string theory in the AdS/CFT correspondence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genus one energy is not dominated by string splitting and joining.
the semi-classical string picture is valid for all values of the coupling constant.
semi-classical splitting and joining is not a dominant contribution to the genus-one string energy shift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the semi-classical string picture is a good approximation to the full string theory.
the semi-classical string picture for the dilatation operator in = 4 SY M is not completely broken down.
the semi-classical string theory is quasilocal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the coherent state formalisation to study string splitting and joining, and to understand the role of the dilatation operator in string theory.
the splitting and joining processes are local in a certain sense.
the splitting and joining of strings is quasilocal in the sense that the splitting or joining process is dominated by a single vertex.
